Rasmus Ristolainen missed most of the season's first six weeks, and since returning he has become a talking point for two reasons. One is the goals: three in 11 games, including one in each of his last two. The other is the market. Broad Street Hockey led with Elliotte Friedman saying no blockbuster will save the Flyers as Ristolainen trade talk grows.

The goals won't hold their pace. They came on 0.93 expected goals, and he's shooting 21% where a typical defenseman sits near 6%. The 98-mph shot, in the 97th percentile, is real, but so is the bigger concern: the Flyers have only 39% of the 5-on-5 chance quality with him on the ice. The case for him is the defending at his own line. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him last season, against 11% for a typical defenseman, and Evolving-Hockey credited most of his value to even-strength defense. He's still playing 18:43 a night, and any team calling will be paying for that, not the shooting.
headline: Rasmus Ristolainen is scoring, and the trade talk is growing
